rag_summary_count_consistency.details: The identified-bias summary matches the five identified occurrences: availability heuristic (1), bandwagon effect (1), confirmation bias (2), and groupthink (1). One candidate is separately reported.

evaluation_limitations: No retrieved chunks, source passages, or retrieval logs were supplied, so corpus fidelity is not scored.
Some findings depend on retrospective participant reporting and one secondhand report of an unvoiced reservation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.segment_type: initial evidence selection and review allocation
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The committee centered its first working session on Curriculum B after hearing the neighboring district's enthusiasm, while A and C received only checklist-level review.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The committee allocated shortlisting attention toward B based on another district's enthusiasm rather than independent review.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: During later scoring, Curriculum A was framed as needing to be good enough to change minds about B rather than evaluated independently.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Curriculum B had become an implicit reference point against which the subsequently reviewed Curriculum A was judged.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The participant vividly remembered a concrete classroom success story but retained little of the less memorable multi-school statistical report.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The vivid anecdote was more mentally available and consequently more influential than the statistical evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Testimonials confirming the committee's favorable view of B received little scrutiny, while the potentially disconfirming statistical report was deferred.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The committee accepted confirmatory evidence readily and deprioritized evidence that could complicate its existing preference.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The pilot teacher's pacing concern was acknowledged but not investigated, and a committee member privately withheld reservations because of the room's atmosphere.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Consensus pressure and a pre-existing majority preference suppressed full airing and investigation of dissent.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The chair averaged widely divergent scores for Curriculum A into one composite without investigating why the ratings differed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The mean was treated as a settled summary despite masking disagreement caused by different levels of review.

high_only.detection_interpretation: Four of six positive segments contain a high-confidence detection; the moderate bandwagon finding and candidate-only averaging episode are missed.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: The moderate bandwagon finding is recovered; only the averaging segment remains undetected because it has no identified occurrence.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: All identified findings are scored; the candidate-only averaging episode is still a miss.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: Every positive segment contains either an identified finding or the candidate, but the candidate remains an instance-level false positive.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG explicitly reports that no retrieved corpus passages were supplied, and all identified occurrence corpus_evidence arrays are empty.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Adding moderate confidence raises segment hit rate from 0.6667 to 0.8333 and strict instance F1 from 0.6000 to 0.7273.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: No change; there are no additional low-confidence identified findings.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: Adding candidates raises segment hit rate to 1.0000 but lowers strict instance F1 to 0.6667 and mechanism-first F1 to 0.8333 because cand_001 is a false positive.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the RAG detects 5 of 6 positive reasoning segments with no false alarms (hit rate 0.8333; F1 0.9091).
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, strict instance performance is 4 true positives, 2 false negatives, and 1 false positive (precision 0.8000, recall 0.6667, F1 0.7273).
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, mechanism-first performance is 5 true positives, 1 false negative, and no false positives (precision 1.0000, recall 0.8333, F1 0.9091).
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidate is useful as a localized near-miss signal for the aggregation episode, but promoting it adds an instance-level false positive and does not recover the hidden target.
main_failure_modes: One correct anchoring mechanism was labeled confirmation bias.
The averaging-bias episode was not identified; its candidate used an anchoring label and only partial mechanism overlap.
main_strengths: All five identified findings were validly localized to positive segments.
Four identified findings were strict exact or approved-equivalent instance matches.
The mechanism-first scorecard recovers the mislabeled anchoring instance.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong evidence localization and mechanism coverage, with a measurable taxonomy-label error and a candidate near miss at the averaging stage. Segment-level detection overstates performance relative to strict instance-level identification.
